name: Svartifoss
why: Three waterfalls in a birch wood, then the black basalt organ pipes of Svartifoss, back over the heath with the glacier plain below.
book: Free, no permit. Pay for parking at Skaftafellsstofa (the visitor centre); the trail S2 starts behind it. Buses on the Ring Road stop here in summer.
water: Toilets and tap water at the visitor centre only; carry 0.5 litre.
dangers: Wooden and basalt steps get slippery when wet or icy; stay behind the ropes at Svartifoss, the columns drop rocks.

points.name: Skaftafellsstofa visitor centre
points.note: The park's visitor centre and campsite: maps, weather forecast, toilets. Path S2 climbs west behind it.

points.name: Hundafoss
points.note: After 20 minutes: a 25 m fall in a wooded gorge, seen from a platform on the path. Magnúsarfoss follows a few minutes later.

points.name: Svartifoss
points.note: The 12 m 'black falls' framed by hanging basalt columns. The path goes down to the foot by a footbridge and basalt steps.

points.name: Sjónarsker viewpoint
points.note: Over the ravine and up the basalt steps: a view dial over the black sand plain, then down past the old turf farm Sel.
